    - First Warden, seven years. The wardens chose me because no one alive knows the gap better. I still take ships through it, when Halvard lets me out of the house.
    - Varro taught me from the age of seven. My mother taught me to argue. Between them they made a pilot.
    - You want to know who I am? Ask who I race. Quenna, Harbour Master of Bain. Twenty-two years ago a squall took her boat's mast off a headland, and we turned back to tow them clear.
    - I threw the line. She caught it. Neither boat finished, the race was void, and we spent the night in a cove eating their bread because ours was wet.
    - Nine wins to her, three to me, four of hers by a length. I buy the first round at the feast more often than I like. Do not repeat that. Everyone already knows it.
    - Ships in, timber out, wool on the quay. Ruan brings me his report every week, and every week it is longer. Bethoc's board says the Strandwood. Torva says the same.
    - Ruan laid it all on my table: Dougal's cord, Gorm's stone, a chewed rope of Kestra's. Something leads the climbers. I want it found, and I want it off my cliffs.
    - The climbers come fewer since the Gapclaw, and less boldly. They have not stopped. I never thought they would. Ruan still wants his lanterns.
    - The Scour is empty and the slack keeps its hour. Whatever else the water is doing, Ailsa will tell me when she is ready. She always has.
    - The inlet. I have read it most of my life, and lately it keeps things from me. The seas are rougher every year.
    - Ailsa's new pages and the old ones do not sit together the way they should. I asked her once. She said not yet. I have not asked again.
    - Your marks agree with Ailsa's pages. So it is not a careless warden, and it is not a strange year. I would almost rather it were.
    - Arlo. He thinks I do not know where he goes at dawn. I am pretending not to. It is a family habit.
    - Mind the steps. They are wet. They are always wet.
    - The lowest tide is our hour. Come. Keep to the high pools.
